metadata.description: `maintenance/reviews.toml` — when each page of a documentation package was last READ ALOUD and by whom, plus the date of the last full reconciliation (PROP-057 `##OBS-MAINTENANCE-TOOLS`, `MAINTENANCE.md` §2.2 and §3). It is authored data and never a generated record: a machine can tell that a citation resolves, and only a person can tell that the prose around it still reads. The file states «when somebody read this», never «what it was checked against» — there are no revisions, hashes or version marks in it, because the seventh edition removed every shape that needed a history (`##OBS-NOTHING-LEAKS`). The order of its rows is also the order of the «page of the week». Source of truth for `crates/vibe-wire/src/generated/doc_reviews/`.

One row per page that has been read aloud at least once, in the order the reading rota visits them. A page with no row has never been read aloud, which the queue reports as exactly that rather than as an age.

The date of the last full reconciliation, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Absent until the first one happens; the queue then counts the days since, against the quarterly promise the team made itself (`MAINTENANCE.md` §2.4).
The page's address inside the package, forward-slashed and relative to the spec root — `model/boot-lane.xml`.
The date it was last read aloud, `YYYY-MM-DD`. A date and not a timestamp: the fact recorded is that somebody sat down with the page on that day, and an hour would be precision nobody has.
Who read it — a name a person recognises, so a queue row can be discussed with the reader.
